title: 1-06 Dark Sea
body:
### Background and Hook(s)

- This is likely the last area explored by the players, and is tailored toward the level bands of 11 - 15 and 13 - 17, meaning creatures with CR maxing out at about 18.
- After this point, the world would be considered "opened up", and the players may choose to return to previous areas that had more substantial challenges (especially in the depths areas of regions).

### Characters and Locations

- 

#### ★12: Blackwater Expanse (Mabar MZ)
 - [ ]  
>The light above you fades to a dull, ashen glow, as though the sea itself were forgetting the sun. The water hangs unnaturally still, flecked with drifting black motes that swallow what little light remains. Pale flakes—like underwater ash—spiral slowly downward into the darkness below. Sound dies quickly here; even movement feels muted and distant. Far beneath, an angular silhouette interrupts the void, silent and unlit.

- Light reduced one step (bright → dim; dim → darkness); water unnaturally still; organic matter desiccates into pale ash that drifts steadily downward toward Hal’mab.
- **The Slow Hunger**. At the end of each minute in the zone, DC 15 Con save or take escalating necrotic damage: 1d6 (minute 1), 2d6 (minute 2), 3d6 (minute 3), increasing by +1d6 each additional minute; resets upon leaving the manifest zone.
- **Ash Consequence**. If reduced to 0 HP by necrotic damage here, the creature immediately dies and crumbles into ash; the ash spirals downward and reforms as a complete corpse upon reaching Hal’mab.
- **Downward Pull**. Each failed Con save against The Slow Hunger causes the creature to descend 20 ft; loose matter constantly drifts downward.
- **Vampire Squid**. A swarm of vampire squid opportunistically attack any creatures who enter this area. They use their mobility to their advantage and try to drain creatures of their life.

`encounter: 4: Vampire Squid`

#### ★12: Hal'mab
 - [ ]  
> There is little but darkness here. There is a structure — a cluster of bone and black coral built against the kar'lassa's dorsal ridge, small enough to miss in the dark, large enough to have taken years. A single dim light burns inside. Something large coils in the water nearby, watching your approach with one enormous eye that catches no reflection.

- Hal'mab is not a sahuagin city. The sahuagin avoid this kar'lassa entirely. What exists here is the result of one kraken priest, a juvenile kraken, and years of Mabar dreams building something with no name and no purpose anyone else would recognize.
- The kar'lassa of Mabar is a leviathan of pitch black scales that absorbs light rather than reflecting it. Its manifest zone imposes two properties on the surrounding water.
- The juvenile kraken came first, drawn to the manifest zone's perpetual darkness and absence of predators or sahuagin interference. It has grown up dreaming in Mabar every night—not hollowed out as mortals are, but shaped. It does not hunt aggressively. It waits. Where the adult in Kraken Bay is overwhelming force and hunger, this creature is patience and extinguishing. It has become, in its alien way, something that feels more like Mabar than like a kraken.
- **Syrrath** came after, drawn to the juvenile kraken as kraken priests are. He arrived with a purpose he has since forgotten. Years of dreaming in Mabar have stripped him of hope, ambition, and the ability to imagine a future. He has not left because leaving requires wanting something elsewhere, and he no longer does. He tends the structure and remains near the juvenile kraken not out of devotion but because it is the only thing that still responds to him—and because, in the kraken's Mabar-shaped stillness, he recognizes something that feels like understanding. They are two creatures that Mabar has made into something similar, sitting in the dark together.
- The Hunger of Mabar is slowly consuming Syrrath. He is aware of this. He does not care.
- Syrrath will speak to the players without hostility, answering questions directly and without evasion. He has nothing left to protect or conceal. He knows the surrounding waters extensively, including Kraken Bay, which he speaks about with the only thing resembling feeling he has left: a hollow awe at the adult kraken that the juvenile will one day become. His description of the lair—the spiral current, the gouged seafloor, the debris field, the shape resting motionless in the deep—is precise, affectless, and more useful than anything the players could find on a map.
- The players may find themselves wanting to help Syrrath. Whether removing him from the manifest zone would restore anything is left unresolved. He will not leave voluntarily. He cannot explain why in terms that satisfy anyone, including himself.
- **The Juvenile Kraken** is not immediately hostile but is protective of Syrrath in the reflexive way of a creature that has imprinted on the only living thing in its territory. Threatening or attacking Syrrath triggers immediate aggression. Approaching with patience allows direct interaction—it is intelligent enough to communicate in limited Aquan if the players attempt it, though its responses are sparse and tend toward the philosophical in a way that unsettles rather than illuminates.

> [!info]- **Eternal Shadows** 
> There is no bright light in Hal'mab. Any object or effect that would usually create bright light only creates dim light instead.

> [!info]- **Radiant Void** 
> In order to cast a spell that deals radiant damage or restores hit points, a creature must succeed on a spellcasting ability check with a DC equal to 10 + the level of the spell. On a failed check, the spell is not cast and its spell slot is not expended, but the action is lost.

`encounter: 1: Kraken Priest, 1: Juvenile Kraken`

##### Characters
- **Syrrath** (N male triton, kraken priest). Lean and colorless, with scales faded to grey-white from years without light. Necrotic discoloration creeps up his forearms in branching patterns, visible to anyone who looks. He has not looked in some time. He moves slowly and speaks in complete, measured sentences with no particular affect. He offers food and a place to rest without warmth or expectation. If asked why he stays, he is quiet for a long moment before saying he no longer remembers what he would return to. He is not lying. He is not performing despair. He is simply a person from whom Mabar has taken the future one dream at a time, leaving someone who functions perfectly and wants nothing.

#### ★12: Mabar Trench
 - [ ]  
> The water darkens by degrees until darkness is no longer the absence of light but a presence of its own. Sound compresses. Movement becomes effort. The pressure here is not a sensation—it is a fact, asserting itself against every joint and surface and breath. The seafloor, if there is one, is not visible. The trench simply continues downward, and the things that live here have learned to be patient about it.

- The Mabar Trench is the deepest point of the Dark Sea, a vertical wound in the seabed that descends beyond any reliable measurement. It exists at the intersection of Mabar's influence and extreme oceanic depth, which makes it the most hostile environment in the campaign short of the planes themselves.
- There is nothing to find here except what the current brings down and what lives on that. Roll on the [[C06 The City Between#Random Discovery|Random Discovery]] table to determine what drifts within reach.
- Vampire squid drift in loose, patient formations at the edge of visibility—filaments extended, moving only when something warm enters their range. They do not rush. They do not need to.
- **Crushing Depth**. The pressure of the trench asserts itself against any creature or vessel not rated for extreme depth. At the start of each round, each affected creature must succeed on a **DC 14 Constitution saving throw** or take **2d10 force damage**. On a success, they take half. Ships that are not purpose-built for extreme depth (seastriders are exempt; elemental submarines and the Nautilux are not) gain **1 Stress** at the start of each round.

`encounter: 3d4: Vampire Squid`

> [!info]- **Eternal Shadows**
> There is no bright light in the Mabar Trench. Any object or effect that would usually create bright light only creates dim light instead.

> [!info]- **Radiant Void**
> In order to cast a spell that deals radiant damage or restores hit points, a creature must succeed on a spellcasting ability check with a DC equal to 10 + the level of the spell. On a failed check, the spell is not cast and its spell slot is not expended, but the action is lost.

#### ★13: Chromatic Bloom (Kythri MZ)
 - [ ]  
>Sunlight fractures across a vast slick of living color, bands of the rainbow drifting just beneath the waves. The water above you shimmers and folds in slow spirals, whole swaths of pigment shearing apart and recombining without pattern. Through a clearer vertical seam in the bloom, you glimpse distant angular shapes far below, distorted by a descending column of prismatic haze. Temperature shifts abruptly as colors slide past one another, and a few groups of creatures can be seen observing the area.

**Chromatic Bands**
- **Red Band**. Extreme heat (DMG rules). Constitution saves vs. exhaustion. Metal surfaces grow dangerously hot.
- **Orange Band**. Viscous bloom layer. Area is difficult terrain; movement speed halved. Propulsion and exposed mechanisms risk fouling.
- **Yellow Band**. High-energy bioluminescent plankton discharge static arcs when disturbed. Con save or take minor lightning damage. Area brightly lit.
- **Green Band**. Toxic algal bloom. Poison gas exposure (Con save vs. poison damage and poisoned condition). Lightly obscured.
- **Blue Band**. Oxygen-rich water. Non-aquatic creatures can breathe normally. Sound carries clearly; Perception checks relying on hearing at advantage.
- **Indigo Band**. Sapphire Jelly (CR 6) colony zone. Nearly invisible except for faint glints; react aggressively to vibration or spellcasting.
- **Violet Band**. Arcane instability. When a spell is cast here, roll on the Wild Magic Surge table.
- **White Band**. Extreme cold (DMG rules). Constitution saves vs. exhaustion. Frost sheets drift in suspended planes.

**Mixing Effects**
Bands are stable when layered. Rapid transition or forced mixing can trigger reactions.
- **Red + Any**. Fire burst; creatures within 20 ft take fire damage. Dex save, `dice:4d6` fire damage on a fail, half on success.
- **Green + Any**. Caustic cloud; acid damage and area heavily obscured for 1 round. Con save, `dice:4d6` acid damage on a fail, half on success.
- **Red + White**. Steam explosion; fire damage plus brief heavily obscured area. Dex save, `dice:5d6` fire damage on a fail, half on success;
- **Yellow + Blue**. Electrical cascade; lightning arcs along metallic surfaces. Dex save, `dice:4d6` lightning damage on a fail, half on success.
Other combinations shift color and temperature without explosive reaction.

**Factions**
- **Hal’Kyth Mage Surveyors**. Planar researchers operating near the chromatic shaft. They chart band stability and harvest specific colors for alchemical use. They offer guided passage through the safer descent path toward the structures below.
- **Kuo-toa Observers**. Small group lingering beyond the outer edge of the bloom, watching its shifting patterns from clear water. They track irregularities in the color spirals as omens. They indicate a recent disturbance—an area where the bands failed to settle—marking the direction of The Pilgrim’s passage.

#### ★13: Hal'kyth
 - [ ]  
>The city never quite holds still. Alchemical clouds drift and change color, structures subtly reshaping as currents shift. The water tastes sharp, then sweet, then bitter in quick succession. Shapes swim past bearing extra fins, altered jaws, or asymmetrical eyes, none of it remarked upon.

- The influence of Kythri supports magic tied to change and transmutation, and these are vital to the society of the Dominion. Hal’kyth is the heart of the alchemical industry. While all great cities harvest the blood of the kar’lassa (as discussed in the next section), it is Hal’kyth that has the greatest capacity for refining it. Though the Dominion is slow to innovate, the artificers of Hal’kyth are an exception, and they continue to develop new techniques; the plasmids discussed in chapter 8 were first magebred in Hal’kyth.
- **Alchemical Activity**. Structured alchemical contests are common here, where participants are given identical base materials and judged on potency, stability, and creative application—explosions are penalized, but not disqualifying.

##### Locations
- **Flux Warrens**. A constantly rearranging lab-complex
- **Vats of Becoming**. Where new strains of magebred are tested—often catastrophically.
- **Spawning Pools**. Eggs are submerged in alchemical instability. Survival rates are appalling. Sahuagin assassins are magebred here, swift and mutable, bred for infiltration and short, lethal deployments.

##### Characters
- **Kethrix Many-Forms** (CN male sahuagin alchemical savant). Kethrix has survived so many mutations that no one remembers his original appearance. He values results over lives, including his own.

#### ✣6: Port Krez (Port)
 - [ ]  
>The harbor comes into view between cliff walls scored with old fire damage and new graffiti. The docks are deep but treacherous — half-sunken hulls visible through the water, close enough to the surface to gut a careless ship. The town beyond is loud, low-built, and lit at all hours. Nobody checks your papers here. Nobody asks where you've been.

- Port Krez is the home port of the Cloudreavers, a pirate principality run on the laws of the sea and little else. It is the closest major port to the Dark Sea and functions as the most accessible black market in the region.
- Unscrupulous merchants know that legitimate trade avoids Port Krez, which means it can be the cheapest place to acquire rare or quasi-legal goods. Prismatic Pearls, stolen PACT manifests, and sahuagin artifacts have all moved through here.
- The Cloudreavers are primarily dwarves, orcs, and half-orcs, many of whom worship the Devourer. Their religious bent makes them unusually aware of — and unsettled by — the strange tides and altered sea life spreading out from the Dark Sea. Sailors here have started refusing certain routes.
- Useful for players who need to fence something, hire muscle without questions, or find information that legitimate ports won't carry. Anything obtained here comes with strings.

##### Characters
- **Prince Mika Rockface** (CE female dwarf, Cloudreaver leader). Commands a fleet of six fast ships and rules Port Krez with the authority of strength alone. Believes herself blessed by the Devourer. She has noticed the sea changing and interprets it as a sign — she's just not sure of what yet. Will deal with the players if they can demonstrate they're worth dealing with.

#### ✣7: Pylas Talaer (Port)
 - [x]  ✅ 2026-03-30
> The dock approach is immaculate. Buildings that have stood ten thousand years line streets kept clean by buried enchantments you can feel humming underfoot. Spectral lights drift overhead carrying messages between towers. The guards at the gate are polite, thorough, and carry themselves like people who have never lost a fight in their city and intend to keep it that way.

- Pylas Talaer is the primary port of contact between Aerenal and the rest of Eberron — more tolerant of outsiders than any other Aereni city, though order is enforced without exception. Every dragonmarked house except House Orien has a presence here.
- Relevant to the campaign as the closest major surface port to Valraean Protectorate waters. Sea elf diplomatic traffic moves through here. Players seeking Valraean contacts, Aereni lore on ancient aquatic civilizations, or access to necromantic scholarship will find leads here.
- Beneath the city lies the Hall of the Bereaved, headquarters of a secret society called the Skullborn — Aereni who have aligned with the Blood of Vol in pursuit of a form of immortality rivaling the Undying Court. This is a slow-burn complication: it has no direct campaign tie, but players who dig into Aereni undead lore or push into restricted areas may surface it uninvited.

##### Characters
- **Governor Syraen Melideth** (LN female elf, wizard). Has governed Pylas Talaer for over a century and is both skilled and ruthless about maintaining order. Known for her skull tattoos and her unusual sympathy toward non-elves, earned through a century of managing a trade port. She is aware of the Valraean Protectorate's tensions with the sahuagin and quietly concerned about what destabilization of the Dark Sea would mean for Aerenal's eastern coast. Will share information with players who approach correctly, and will not share it with players who don't.

#### ♦1: Valraean Protectorate
 - [x]  ✅ 2026-03-30
> The city rises from the seabed in tiered white stone, each level older and more precisely maintained than the one above it. Gold inlay catches the ambient light and throws it back in long lines across the surrounding water. Undying soldiers stand at intervals along the outer walls — motionless, iridescent, older than most surface civilizations. The sea elves who pass them offer a slight incline of the head. No one else is expected to know the custom, but everyone is watched to see if they do.

- The Protectorate's seat has no canon name. It is called **Shae Valaer** here — "Valaer's Rest" in the Aereni tradition of naming cities after their founders — though sea elves refer to it simply as the Protectorate when speaking to outsiders.
- The city is structured on Aereni civic principles: tiered by lineage, governed through a mix of living administrators and deathless advisors, and oriented entirely around the Undying Court's authority. Undying soldiers patrol the outer walls and undying councilors consult with scholars and advise living administrators. The presence of the deathless here is less concentrated than in Shae Mordai but unmistakable.
- Locathah fill service and labor roles throughout the city. This is not presented as exploitation — it is framed as a structured relationship with clear obligations on both sides, and most sea elves genuinely believe it. The locathah who work here are housed, fed, and protected. They are also not free to leave without completing their contracted term, and the terms are set by the Protectorate. The distinction between contract and captivity is one the city has chosen not to examine.
- The most sacred civic rite is trance communion, in which sea elves connect to the gestalt consciousness of the Undying Court. Non-elves cannot participate and are not expected to understand it, but the hours during which it occurs — dawn and dusk — are treated as near-sacred quiet time throughout the city. Visitors who disrupt this are not punished; they are simply remembered.
- Freedom of religion is not permitted within the Protectorate. Devotion to the Undying Court is civic law, not merely custom. Kuo-toa cult activity in Protectorate waters is treated as a criminal and spiritual matter simultaneously, handled by the Priests of Transition rather than the city guard.

##### Locations
- **The Tiered Court.** The administrative and judicial center of the city, built in the step-pyramid style of Aereni temples but adapted for underwater construction — wider, lower, and ringed with current baffles that keep the surrounding water still. Walls are engraved with the histories of the deathless councilors who serve as the city's patrons. Living administrators hear cases and receive petitions in the outer tiers; deathless advisors occupy the inner chambers, consulted on matters of precedent and long-term consequence.
- **The Chapel of Transition.** The ritual that transforms a living elf into one of the undying can only be performed in a sanctioned space. The Protectorate maintains one such chapel, smaller and more austere than those in Shae Mordai, used rarely but maintained as if it might be needed at any moment. Priests of Transition staff it permanently. Non-elves are not permitted inside under any circumstances.
- **The Chronicle Vault.** When an elf dies, two records of their life are written — one interred with them, one kept in the great library. The Protectorate's vault holds copies of every chronicle produced since the city's founding, as well as patrol records, diplomatic correspondence, and intelligence on regional threats going back centuries. Players with legitimate standing and a compelling reason may be granted limited access. The deathless archivist who manages it has been doing so for over two thousand years and has opinions about everything.
- **The Undying Garrison.** The Protectorate's military quarter, where living patrol captains coordinate with undying soldiers who have served since the city's founding. The garrison tracks sahuagin movement, Abyssal Protectorate activity, and — increasingly — unusual behavior among the kuo-toa population in the surrounding waters. Reports have been accumulating that no one has yet decided how to act on.

##### Characters
- **High Warden Thessavel ir'Valraea** (LN female sea elf, administrator). Tall and unhurried in the way of someone who has never been made to hurry. She administers Protectorate law and fleet operations with complete confidence in their legitimacy. She is not cruel — she is indifferent to the distinction between order and justice, which produces the same outcomes. She will engage players formally and without hostility so long as they treat the Protectorate's authority as real. She will not negotiate on matters she considers settled, and she considers most matters settled.
- **Undying Councilor Aevrath** (N male deathless sea elf, advisor). One of the city's founding generation, preserved and still advising. He speaks slowly and rarely, and when he does the room adjusts. He has watched the Protectorate evolve from a military outpost into a civilization and has complicated feelings about what it has become. Players who earn an audience with him — which requires Thessavel's approval — will find someone who answers questions with uncomfortable precision and occasionally asks questions back that suggest he already knows the answers.

#### ♦1: Abyssal Protectorate
 - [x]  ✅ 2026-03-30
- The home of Cordelia and her sect that protects the fragile depths of the seas. Siberys shards (fallen from the skies above) are common here, and recently attention has been drawn to them by the denizens of the land.
- Dragonmarked House ships have been spotted here recently, undersea crawlers that appear to be collaborations between House Lyrandar and House Cannith.

#### ⚔4: Dark Sea
 - [ ]  
- Ancestral giants from the nearby continent of Xen'drik and ancient monstrosities from the depths intermingle in the shadowy waters of this sea.

| --: | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
|   1 | **Dragon Turtle, Dread Wake (CR 17)**. A mountain-backed silhouette rises from absolute darkness, superheated currents boiling the surrounding water. It attacks immediately, asserting dominance over a migration lane that has claimed countless ships.<br>`encounter: 1: Dragon Turtle`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
|   2 | **Adult Sea Dragon, Blackwater Tyrant (CR 18)**. The dragon coils out of the dark with deliberate calm, scales drinking in light. It attacks immediately, shaping crushing waves and frigid pressure to control the battlefield.<br>`encounter: 1: Adult Sea Dragon`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|   3 | **Krake Spawn Hunting Pair (CR ~15–16)**. Massive limbs unfurl from opposite sides of the ship, striking in coordinated patterns meant to immobilize and tear apart prey before it can flee.<br>`encounter: 2: Krake Spawn`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|   4 | **Illhveli, Nauthveli — Shadow Leviathan (CR 16)**. The whale’s bulk emerges slowly, water darkening unnaturally around it. Once it commits, it rams with terrifying momentum, dragging everything nearby into its wake.<br>`encounter: 1: Nauthveli Illhveli`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|   5 | **Shoal Ooze Blackout (CR ~15)**. Light dies abruptly as oily darkness spreads through the water. The patches smother vision while the ooze flows in as a single, suffocating mass, attacking immediately.<br>`encounter: 1: Shoal Ooze, 2: Black Patch`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|   6 | **Reef Drake Shadow Ambush (CR ~14)**. Jagged reef spires rise into the dark like broken teeth. The drakes burst from concealment, using the terrain to break lines of sight and strike from multiple angles.<br>`encounter: 2: Reef Drake`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|   7 | **Breakwater Troll Crossing (CR ~13–14)**. The trolls cling to a collapsed causeway barely visible in the gloom. They attack immediately, attempting to drag targets into crushing depths where regeneration favors them.<br>`encounter: 2: Breakwater Troll`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|   8 | **Brain Coral of the Sunken Silence (CR ~14–15)**. A massive coral mass pulses faintly with bioluminescent thought. Psychic pressure builds as the drakes herd intruders closer, and the coral lashes out to dominate and disorient.<br> `encounter: 1: Brain Coral, 2: Reef Drake`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|   9 | **Graknork at the Black Shoals (CR 14)**. The water ahead brightens slightly with reflected light from a field of shattered stone spires. At their center hangs a vast, armored silhouette slowly turning in the current, old hull plates and anchors embedded in its carapace. Debris drifts inward like a tide. <br>Hostility triggers: steering toward the shoals, attempting to pass through the debris field, using loud or forceful magic, or remaining within visual range for more than 2 rounds. Once provoked, the graknork surges forward to crush the ship against the rocks.<br>`encounter: 1: Graknork` |
|  10 | **Timingila in the Lightless Drift (CR 15)**. The surrounding water grows unnaturally still as light fades faster than it should. A vast shape moves just beyond perception, circling without sound.<br>Hostility triggers: using bright or shadow-aligned magic, sharply altering course toward the disturbance, or remaining in the area for more than 2 rounds. If triggered, the timingila strikes from total darkness and fights to keep prey disoriented and isolated.<br> `encounter: 1: Timingila`                                                                                                            |

#### ⚔4: Kuo-toa Settlement/Ruins
 - [ ]  
> The ruins open gradually as you approach — spires of ancient stone webbed with coral growth, structures too deliberate to be natural and too worn to be recent. Kuo-toa move through the water between them without urgency, watching your approach with wide, unblinking eyes. From somewhere deeper in the city, a sound reaches you: low, layered harmonics, dozens of voices producing a tone that makes the water itself vibrate against your skin. It resolves into itself and begins again, never ending.

- The settlement occupies the upper tier of a drowned city that predates the current age by millennia. The kuo-toa here are descended from escaped Tidecrown laborers who built a community inside ruins they understood to be ancestral — but not what those ancestors actually were.
- The city reads in three vertical layers. The living settlement and Coral Stage sit at the top; the ancient ruined city below it; and the cult space at the lowest accessible level. Iconography shifts with each layer: **indigo and silver** dominate above, fading to **violet over silver** in the cult space, where the original carvings have been overlaid rather than destroyed.
- The Pilgrim passed through here. Its influence is the direct cause of the cult presence. Players who have encountered the Pilgrim elsewhere will find corroborating details in what Ssiveth describes.
- If the **Kuo-toa faction clock** is advanced, the cult presence in the lower layer is larger and more organized, and Ssiveth is visibly distressed with diminishing influence over his own settlement. The cult has been thinning out since the Pilgrim moved on — the most committed members have followed it, leaving recent converts and a rearguard of true believers.

##### Locations
- **The Coral Stage.** A broad bowl of ancient stone colonized by generations of coral growth, its shape focusing sound in a way that feels almost designed. The concert takes place here — dozens of kuo-toa producing recursive harmonics that carry through the entire city. Ssiveth approaches players here. A DC 14 Insight or Arcana check reveals the harmonic is structured as a repeated signal, not a performance. Any creature that remains for 10 minutes must succeed on a **DC 12 Wisdom save** or receive a vision: the city intact, kuo-toa moving freely between water and a silver-lit plane, then the sky fracturing and the light going dark. The vision is a memory of when the city was sundered and separated from Dal Quor by the actions of the ancient Giants.
- **The Ruined City.** Beneath the settlement, the ancient city is intact enough to read as a civilization. Civic buildings, a cartographic archive, devotional structures. The kuo-toa depicted in carvings are visually identical to modern kuo-toa. Silver inlay throughout depicts Dal Quor as a neighboring plane — spirals the kuo-toa moved through freely, most of the inlay stripped out and leaving pale ghost-impressions in the stone. One panel depicts the severance: the sky fracturing, the spirals going dark, the population turning on itself. A player who can read ancient Kuo-toa, or succeeds on a **DC 16 History check** with time to study the archive, learns that the Giants' severance of Dal Quor didn't merely cut off a plane — it severed the kuo-toa from the cognitive and spiritual architecture that made their civilization function.
- **The Cult Space.** The deepest accessible layer. Violet dominates; silver appears only as thin accent lines; indigo is nearly absent. The spiral motif from the levels above reappears here — same shape, inverted, pressed in violet-stained coral over the original carvings. The harmonic from the Coral Stage filters down through the city and is strongest here. Players who saved above must save again at **DC 15** after 10 minutes. Cult members present are not immediately hostile but do not welcome observation. Combat is likely if the players linger or interfere.

`encounter: 1d6: Deep One Cultist, 1: Deep One Priest`

##### Characters
- **Ssiveth** (N male kuo-toa, settlement elder). Pale grey-green skin faded with age, eyes clouded but sharp. Speaks careful, deliberate Common learned over decades of negotiating with Tidecrown officials who never learned Kuo-toa in return. He founded this settlement and is proud of it. He is also frightened of what it is becoming. Ssiveth is a direct biological descendant of the pre-severance civilization — an unbroken lineage from before the Giants severed Dal Quor. He does not know this. He knows his family line is old and that he dreams more vividly than most, but has no framework to interpret it. He is the inverse of the Pilgrim: where the Pilgrim's dormant connection has been violently reawakened and bent toward the Deep One, Ssiveth's is intact and uncorrupted. He will speak freely about the ruins, the Pilgrim's passage, and his fears about the concerts. He will not ask players to go below, but will also not stop them.

#### ⚔5: Dragonreach
 - [ ]  
- The territory of the Maraen Sea Elves, the area north of the Dark Sea (between Argonnesson and Aerenal) is known as Dragonreach.

| d10 | Encounter                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| --: | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
|   1 | **Adult Sea Dragon, Border Tyrant (CR 18)**. The dragon rises openly from below, coils cutting deliberate arcs through the water. It attacks immediately, enforcing ancient territorial claims that predate modern elven patrols.<br>`encounter: 1: Adult Sea Dragon`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|   2 | **Adult Bronze Dragon, Sentinel of the Reach (CR 15)**. The dragon approaches from above and below in sweeping passes, crackling with restrained lightning. It attacks immediately, testing the party’s strength and intent through force before allowing any passage.<br>`encounter: 1: Adult Bronze Dragon`                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|   3 | **Draconic Patrol Wing (CR ~15–16)**. The drakes herd and harass while the serpent commits to crushing strikes, a practiced patrol pattern meant to drive intruders away from Argonnesson-facing routes.<br>_1× Young Sea Serpent (CR 8), 2× Reef Drake (CR 9)._                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
|   4 | **Dragon Eel Kill-Current (CR 12)**. #### ⚔5: Dragon Turtle Feeding/Breeding Grounds
 - [ ]  
> The water here is warmer than it should be, thick with the smell of sulfur and something older — fat, briny, organic. Schools of giant tuna move in slow rotation around a central thermal vent, too dense to see through cleanly. Below them, half-buried in the seabed sediment, a cluster of objects the size of boulders pulses with faint heat. The cave mouth to the east is dark, but the gold inside catches even this light and throws it back in a dull, scattered gleam. Whatever lives here is not here right now. The feeding schools suggest it will not be gone long.

- The feeding ground centers on a thermal vent that draws enormous concentrations of tuna, giant squid, and whale-sized prey fish. The vent keeps the surrounding water several degrees warmer than the Dark Sea baseline, creating a visible thermal boundary at the area's edge.
- The clutch sits in the open sediment near the vent, partially buried for warmth — seven eggs, each roughly four feet across, shells thick and ridged. They are close enough to hatching that fine cracks are visible along the upper surfaces. Interfering with the clutch — moving, damaging, or taking an egg — immediately escalates the adult's return clock by one step.
- The cave to the east is the adult's den and contains the accumulated wreckage of decades of destroyed ships: gold coins, trade bars, broken dragonmarks still embedded in hull fragments, and personal effects from crews that didn't survive. The total value is substantial — `dice: 10d10*100` gp in recoverable coin and trade goods, plus `dice: 1d6` minor magic items salvaged from wrecks.
- **The Clock.** The adult left recently — evidence includes a fresh gouge in the seabed and a half-consumed whale carcass still bleeding into the water. At the end of every 10 minutes the players spend in the area, advance the clock one step. At step 3, a distant rumble carries through the water. At step 5, the feeding schools scatter. At step 6, the adult arrives.

> [!info]- **Thermal Instability**
> The vent causes unpredictable surges. At the start of each round within 60 feet of it, roll a d6. On a 1, a surge vents scalding water in a 20-foot radius — each creature in range must succeed on a **DC 13 Dexterity save** or take **2d6 fire damage**, half on a success.

`encounter: 1: Dragon Turtle`
